The public education system wasn't and isn't the most effective and encouraging for poor learners to want to thrive academically. I was always absent at school because I'd rather be at home and watch anime all day. (didn't know it was a defense mechanism back then)

Despite my absences no teacher had actually confronted me or informed my parents about it, and I do not blame them. We were about 120 students in one cramped classroom that turns into an oven passed 12 noon. I remember two of my classmates fainted only in the first week of school

I would probably study languages abroad. Make myself more fluent in the English language, study music, pursue a more expensive degree that has a relation to one of my interests. Most of my peers in high school are now minimum wage earners and only a few got a degree.

I guess I was lucky becoz I got offered a full scholarship in a small city college in my hometown although I wasn't really the most outstanding student in high school. In fact, it's quite the opposite as my high school GPA didn't even reach their minimum requirement for my degree

I just know that the dean who interviewed me was just really convinced I was being sincere when I bullshited my way to ace that entrance interview. I know he's the reason why I got a full scholarship and the exam results too of course.

I know a lot of people who stopped study becoz they couldn't afford the fees. again we are a third world country, what you may consider as a small amount could probably worth months of their or their parents salary. And education isn't the only thing they have to spend on.
